questions.q: You build `list.stream().filter(p).map(f)` and never call a terminal operation. What happens?
o: Nothing runs: intermediate operations are lazy
The pipeline runs and results are discarded
The pipeline runs and the list is modified
It does not compile without a terminal call
questions.w: Streams are lazy. Only a terminal operation such as `collect`, `count` or `forEach` triggers the work.

questions.q: What happens if you call a terminal operation twice on the same stream?
o: `IllegalStateException`: the stream was already operated upon
The second call returns the same result again
The second call returns an empty result
The stream restarts from the first element
questions.w: Streams are single-use. Call `stream()` on the source again for another pass.

questions.q: A stream of customers, each with a list of accounts. Which operation yields one flat `Stream<Account>`?
o: `flatMap(c -> c.accounts().stream())`
`map(Customer::accounts)`
`filter(c -> !c.accounts().isEmpty())`
`collect(Collectors.toList())`
questions.w: `map` gives a `Stream<List<Account>>`. `flatMap` flattens the inner streams into one.

questions.q: `Collectors.toMap(Account::branch, Account::id)` is used on accounts where two share a branch. What happens?
o: `IllegalStateException` for the duplicate key
The second value silently replaces the first
Both values are stored in a list
The duplicate is skipped and the stream continues
questions.w: `toMap` fails on duplicates unless you give a merge function, or use `groupingBy` to collect all values per key.

questions.q: Which collector splits accounts into exactly two groups, active and inactive?
o: `partitioningBy(Account::isActive)`
`groupingBy(Account::branch)`
`toMap(Account::id, Account::isActive)`
`counting()`
questions.w: `partitioningBy` always returns a map with both a `true` and a `false` key. `groupingBy` can have any number of keys.

questions.q: Which parallel stream use is the most likely to be correct and fast?
o: A pure CPU-heavy computation over a large `ArrayList`
Calling a remote service for each element
Adding results to a shared `ArrayList` from the lambda
Streaming a tiny list of five elements
questions.w: Parallel streams use the shared common pool and need stateless, CPU-bound work on large, splittable data. Always measure.

questions.q: What is the difference between `reduce` and `collect`?
o: `collect` is a mutable reduction into a container, `reduce` folds into one value
`reduce` builds lists and maps, `collect` only adds numbers
`reduce` is lazy and `collect` is eager
They are the same operation with different names
questions.w: Building a list with `reduce` copies it at every step. `collect` is designed for containers and is parallel-safe.

questions.q: Why is `peek` a poor place for required logic?
o: It may not run at all, for example after short-circuiting or when the size is known
It always runs twice for each element
It modifies the elements of the source
It forces the stream to become parallel
questions.w: `peek` exists mainly for debugging. Required side effects belong in a terminal operation such as `forEach`.
